source_review.notes: Reviewed MIT 6.006 BST and balancing lectures, Princeton Algorithms BST material, Open Data Structures unbalanced BST chapter, Software Foundations SearchTree verification chapter, current ISO C++ ordering and associative requirements, current Rust BTreeMap documentation, current OpenJDK TreeMap source, and current Linux rbtree documentation. All ten final destinations returned HTTP 200. Plain-BST claims are separated from balanced production-tree API and implementation observations.

evidence: Checked n,h,x.left,x.right,x.parent,open lower/upper bounds,comparator equivalence,search path,transplant,association-copy, and node-transplant terminology.
Checked height convention is node-height: empty zero, leaf one, longest root-to-leaf node count.
Checked strict comparisons and equivalence are used consistently for a unique-key ordered map.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Duplicate-key/multimap placement is intentionally excluded unless a separate policy is supplied.

evidence: Reconstructed insertion of 8,3,10,1,6,14,4,7,13 and confirmed in-order keys 1,3,4,6,7,8,10,13,14 and height four.
Confirmed updating key 6 leaves size nine and changes its value to SIX_UPDATED.
Confirmed deleting leaf 7, one-child node 14 by promoting 13, and two-child node 3 using successor 4 leaves 1,4,6,8,10,13.
Recomputed final size six, root eight, node-height three, lookup 6=SIX_UPDATED, and exact eleven-line trace.
numerical_recomputation.notes: An initial trace order was rejected because deleting key 1 first had reduced node 3 to a one-child case; the corrected trace genuinely exercises all three deletion shapes.

evidence: Verified search interval refinement excludes the opposite subtree under the global BST invariant.
Verified insertion at the failed-search null link satisfies all inherited ancestor bounds and update preserves structure/count.
Verified null/one-child promotion stays inside the deleted node's inherited interval.
Verified successor is right-subtree minimum with no left child; after detachment, left keys are below successor and remaining right keys above it.
Verified path operations are O(h), full traversal Theta(n), and the plain invariant permits h=n.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: No random-input average-height or balancing theorem is used to strengthen the worst-case contract.

evidence: Reviewed empty/singleton, root/non-root leaf, only-left/only-right, two children with immediate/deep successor, successor right child, missing key, minimum, maximum, and root deletion.

Reviewed sorted/reverse degeneration, recursion depth, comparator-equivalent objects, mutable/inconsistent/reentrant/failing comparison, key/value construction/assignment failure, and duplicate policy.
Reviewed parent pointers, association versus node identity, intrusive/pool nodes, iterator mutation/cancellation, clear/destruction depth, serialization corruption, and untrusted shape.
Reviewed structural concurrency, link publication, reader lifetime, external locking, version/fail-fast limits, reclamation, and resource caps.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: A plain BST must not accept unbounded adversarial depth while relying on recursive stack behavior.

evidence: Checked global open ancestor bounds rather than immediate-child comparisons.
Checked finite unique reachability by node identity and reachable count equals size.
Checked each insertion/update/deletion preserves strict in-order keys and exact values in the finite trace.
Checked the association-copy implementation explicitly makes no stable node-handle promise.
invariant_checking.notes: The executable checker has no parent pointers, augmentation, generic comparator, injected failure, or concurrency state to validate.

evidence: Reviewed exact lookup, lower/upper bound candidate retention, min/max, predecessor/successor, and range-traversal reasoning.
Reviewed leaf, one-child, association-copy successor deletion, and physical transplant as distinct structural/lifetime proofs.
Reviewed explicit-stack and parent-pointer traversal costs and invalidation obligations.
Reviewed why comparator law, allocation/publication ordering, count changes, and exact destruction belong to the operation proof.
proof_review.notes: AVL/red-black height guarantees, rotations, and concurrent BST algorithms retain separate proof obligations in later modules.

evidence: MIT, Princeton, Open Data Structures, and Software Foundations support plain-BST academic/proof claims.
Rust BTreeMap, OpenJDK TreeMap, Linux rbtree, and the second MIT lecture are explicitly labeled balanced production/academic contrasts.
Worst-case O(h), worst-case O(n), balanced O(log n), empirical cost, stack space, and amortized traversal statements are separated.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Current library behavior is not presented as an implementation of the executable unbalanced tree.

evidence: The standard-library Python mutation trace passed exact eleven-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status under the recorded toolchain.
It emits evidence=finite_bst_mutation_trace and checks update, leaf/one-child/two-child erase, in-order output, root, size, height, global bounds, and unique reachability.
All ten final source destinations and all repository-local links were checked directly.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No named library/kernel tree, generic comparator, parent links, iterator invalidation, allocation/value failure, deep stack, balanced height, concurrent history, cache/memory profile, or benchmark was empirically evaluated.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed ordered-map semantics, comparator equivalence, global bounds, search/insert/navigation, deletion identity choices, iteration, height degeneration, recursion, ownership, concurrency, testing, and benchmark interpretation.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed construct-before-link insertion, staged/failure-aware update, root/parent rewiring, successor-right-child preservation, node-handle matrix, iterative depth controls, comparator reentrancy, intrusive/pool ownership, external synchronization, logical serialization, observability, and entry/depth/comparison/allocation/time limits.

pedagogical_review.notes: Establishes the unbalanced BST as a proof baseline before balancing, derives every ordered operation from one global invariant, contrasts association-copy and node-transplant deletion, includes a corrected reproduced mutation trace, twelve misconceptions, ten examples, and five progressive exercises with complete answers.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary-source, mathematical, executable-snippet, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic, MIT/Princeton/Software Foundations, Rust/OpenJDK/Linux maintainer, security, performance, reliability, operations, architecture, or independent practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and finite trace prove neither balanced/logarithmic worst-case height, a generic strict-weak-order implementation, exception/lifetime safety for arbitrary payloads, stable node handles, recursion safety for unbounded depth, thread safety, concurrent linearizability, safe reclamation, production memory/cache behavior, benchmark superiority, certification, nor deployment fitness.
